title: The Briefing
tagline: AI intelligence for Gauntlet AI — May 4, 2026

items.headline: Nvidia unveils Nemotron 3 Nano Omni multimodal model
items.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts open-weights multimodal model consolidating vision, audio, and language processing into a single system for AI agents. It achieves up to 9x higher throughput than competing open models while maintaining interactive responsiveness, addressing a real bottleneck in agent systems. The model tops six leaderboards for document intelligence and video/audio understanding. Launched April 28 via Hugging Face, OpenRouter, and 25+ partner platforms with early adoption from Palantir, H Company, Foxconn, and others building production agents.

items.headline: xAI updates Grok with lower prices and expanded context handling
items.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.3 at $1.25 per million input tokens—approximately 37.5% cheaper than Grok 4.2. The model runs reasoning permanently rather than as an optional mode, and handles a one-million-token context window. It can autonomously generate Excel spreadsheets, PDFs, and PowerPoint decks, plus access web search and code execution. On benchmarks, Grok 4.3 still lags OpenAI and Anthropic's latest models, though it improves over its predecessor. xAI also released Custom Voices for voice cloning and the voice agent API at $3/hr (US only, outside Illinois).

items.headline: OpenAI publishes operating principles on path to AGI
items.summary: OpenAI published a statement of operating principles to guide its work toward artificial general intelligence: democratization (resisting power consolidation), empowerment (enabling users to accomplish valuable tasks), universal prosperity (ensuring broad economic benefit), resilience (collaborating on safety and societal risks), and adaptability (updating positions as technology evolves). The company explicitly flags that future trade-offs may force it to prioritize resilience over empowerment. The statement reveals reasoning behind unusual business decisions—massive compute spending despite modest revenue, vertical integration, and global datacenter expansion—which OpenAI frames as expressions of belief in universal prosperity rather than standard growth tactics.

items.headline: IBM releases Granite 4.1 model suite with multilingual and multimodal variants
items.summary: IBM released Granite 4.1, a collection spanning language, vision, speech, embedding, and safety models—its broadest model release to date. Language models come in 3B, 8B, and 30B parameter sizes, and IBM claims the new 8B instruct model matches or beats its previous 32B mixture-of-experts model, a meaningful efficiency jump for teams watching inference costs. All three are trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a multi-stage reinforcement learning pipeline separately targeting instruction following, conversation quality, and mathematical reasoning. The speech line includes a non-autoregressive variant (Granite Speech 4.1 2B NAR) generating entire sequences at once rather than one token at a time, trading some transcription features for substantially higher GPU throughput. Granite Guardian 4.1 expands the prior guardrail model's risk taxonomy and is designed to run alongside any LLM—open or proprietary—as an inline safety layer. All models released under Apache 2.0.

items.headline: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni powers production agent deployment
items.summary: Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Nano Omni consolidates multimodal processing for AI agents with 9x throughput improvements over competitors. Already in production use at Palantir and others.

items.headline: Tech giants acknowledge AI's environmental strain, challenging CO2 pledges
items.summary: Tech giants including Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft acknowledged AI's strain on the environment, challenging their CO2 pledges as massive compute spending for AI infrastructure scales globally.

items.headline: Kimi K2.6 challenges leading open-weights models
items.summary: Kimi K2.6 matches or beats open Qwen3.6 Max and DeepSeek V4, though it falls just behind top closed models.

items.headline: Researchers model human decision-making in Rock-Paper-Scissors with LLMs
items.summary: Researchers at UT-Austin and Google modeled human decision-making in Rock-Paper-Scissors to compare strategic thinking in LLMs versus humans.
